models.notes: Wanderer hero ship, nose along Godot -Z (Blender +Y), origin = centre of mass, 1 unit = 1 m. Scene root = importer node named after the file, its only child is `Ship` (empty at the origin); every other node is a flat child of `Ship`. AABB excludes the engine glow cones (size above = hull + gear incl. deployed gear; base_y = lowest foot pad). ENGINE GLOW: EngineGlow_L/R origin = centre of the nozzle exit plane; the node is rotated (-90 deg about Blender X) so that its LOCAL -Y axis points to the rear of the ship; the cone mesh runs along local -Y (length 2.8 m, radius 0.6 m at the nozzle). Scale the node's local Y (scale.y, 0..1.2) for thrust; x/z scale = flame width. Two surfaces: surface0 translucent outer (alpha 0.45), surface1 hot inner core. GEAR (exported deployed, hinge point = node origin): Gear_Front retracts by rotating about local X by -90 deg (rotation.x = -PI/2, folds aft into the belly); Gear_L rotates about local Z by +90 deg, Gear_R about local Z by -90 deg (rotation.z = +/-PI/2; both fold inward into the engine nacelles / wing roots) [deviation from the spec text: side gear uses local Z (= Blender Y, longitudinal) instead of local Y, a vertical axis cannot lift a foot]. Fully retracted nothing sticks out of the hull. Foot contact points: Anchor_GearContact_* at y=-1.90 (deployed). RAMP: RampDoor is the left (-X) boarding hatch, hinge = bottom edge of the hatch (origin (-1.51,-0.55,-1.36)); open it by rotating about local Z by +90 deg (rotation.z = +PI/2): it swings out/down into a horizontal ramp pointing to -X. CANOPY: translucent blue glass (alpha 0.35, BLEND) over `CockpitInterior` (seat, sticks, dash with emissive screens); the glass is single sided so the cockpit camera sees through it. ANCHORS (Godot coords, relative to Ship): Anchor_ChaseCam (0,4.5,16), Anchor_Cockpit (0,1.15,-2.75) eye point looking along -Z, Anchor_Exit (-3.3,-1.9,-1.36) ground point beside the left door, Anchor_Engine_L/R (+-1.95,0.02,6.8) emitter points 0.35 m behind the nozzles, Anchor_GearContact_Front (0,-1.9,-3.51), _L (-3.3,-1.9,2.3), _R (3.3,-1.9,2.3). NavLight_L (red, port/-X wingtip), NavLight_R (green), NavLight_Tail (white): small emissive spheres, blink by toggling visibility / material emission. Hull has 6 material slots: ship_player_hull (warm white), _dark (graphite underside), _accent (orange), _metal, _glow (cyan strips/engine core), _trim (grey). Tintable: swap ship_player_accent for another colour.

Decorative capital cargo ship ~148 m long (size[2]; nose along Godot -Z, origin mid-ship; bridge tower at the rear). Root `Freighter`; children Hull, Containers (6 colour slots), Engines, EngineGlow_0..4 (same convention as the Wanderer: origin = nozzle exit plane, node rotated so LOCAL -Y points astern, mesh runs along local -Y, scale.y = flame length, base length 24 m x scale (centre engine r=3.3 m, the four outer ones 0.66x)), NavLight_L/R/Tail, BlinkLight and BlinkLight_2 (red beacons on the masts). AABB excludes the glow cones. Windows are emissive (ship_freighter_window).

Orbital station ~217 m across. Root `Station`; children Hub (stationary: body, docking arms, antennas), Ring (habitat wheel + 6 spokes, origin = hub centre), SolarPanels, NavLight_L/R, BlinkLight, Anchor_Dock. STATION AXIS = Blender Y = Godot Z (the docking bay at the front tip faces Godot -Z). SPIN `Ring` about its LOCAL Z axis in Godot (rotate_object_local(Vector3.BACK, angle)); about 0.01-0.03 rad/s looks right. Anchor_Dock = centre of the front docking port (0,0,-63) looking out along -Z. Windows are emissive (station_orbital_window), ring windows are on the +-Z faces and outer face.

Small comms satellite ~7 m span, origin at the centre of the bus. Root `Satellite`; children Body (gold-foil bus, dish pointing toward -Z/+Y, antennas), SolarPanels (spin/tilt if wanted), BlinkLight (red emissive sphere on a mast, origin at the sphere centre; toggle visibility to blink).

Asteroid fragment (lumpy elongated potato, 8 craters), flat shaded low-poly, origin at the centre (centre of mass; the AABB centre is up to ~3 m off it). Root `Asteroid_Root` > `Asteroid` (4 materials: asteroid_rock_dark / asteroid_rock_mid / asteroid_rock_light = three-tone rock patches, all tintable via 'rock'; asteroid_ore = raised metallic ore veins with pinched ends).
